sentences.text: Watsonosteus was a small placoderm, an extinct armored fish, that averaged 57 cm in length, though some reached one meter. It is one of the few arthrodire genera known from complete body fossils.
The genus was described by Miles and Westoll in 1963. The type species, Watsonosteus fletti, was originally described by Watson in 1932.

This animal belongs to the class Placodermi and is classified as an extinct coccosteid arthrodire. It sits within the family Coccosteidae, part of the clade Coccosteomorphi inside the group Eubrachythoraci.

Fossils of Watsonosteus date from 387.95 to 382.31 million years ago, living during the Late Givetian stage of the Middle Devonian period. These remains have been found in the Orkney Islands, Scotland.
